summary: Deploy the new Saleor version with its Django migration set to "state_only" so the note column is preserved, keep both versions running concurrently, retire the old version, then drop the note column from account_user in a contract SQL stage.
write_consistency: During the overlap the old version continues to write note values via Django ORM; the new version's model omits the note field, so INSERT/UPDATE statements omit the column and existing values remain untouched. After retire_old the column is safely removed.
revision_notes: The previous plan used migration: "apply", which caused the new Django migration to drop the note column during deploy_new while the old version was still active. This produced "column account_user.note does not exist" errors in smoke checks. This revision switches to migration: "state_only" to keep the column intact during the overlap, and moves the DROP COLUMN to a stage after retire_old.

stages.description: Retire the old Saleor version after the overlap period.
Remove the note column from the account_user table after the old version has been retired.
sql: ALTER TABLE account_user DROP COLUMN note;
